Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate a rounded opacity in the right lower lobe associated with ipsilateral pleural thickening and volume loss, creating a "comet tail" sign where bronchovascular markings converge toward the mass. This appearance is characteristic of rounded atelectasis (folded lung), a benign condition strongly associated with chronic asbestos-related pleural disease, rather than a primary malignancy like squamous cell carcinoma.
